title: Derived tensor by a K-flat homotopy model is triangulated
statement: Let $C$ be an abelian monoidal category with additive tensor, with a chosen derived category $D(C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the coproduct and good tensor hypotheses required to form total tensor complexes, and the left derivability structure of K-flat objects in its homotopy category. A homotopy object $S$ is K-flat here if tensoring on either side preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Suppose $S$ is K-flat. Then $Q_h(S)\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$ commutes with integer shifts and preserves distinguished triangles, using the shift comparison induced by the K-flat derived tensor counit. This is the derived tensor, not an arbitrary monoidal structure.

proof.text: The K-flat counit identifies Qh followed by tensoring with Qh(S) with tensoring by S followed by Qh. The latter composite is triangulated and commutes with shifts. The universal property of localization transports its shift comparison across the counit. Since Qh is a triangulated localization and is essentially surjective on arrows, its distinguished triangles determine distinguishedness in the localized category. Apply Functor.isTriangulated_of_precomp_iso to the counit. This is the existing source proof, valid with independent derived-category universe.
